title: Unloading document steps run twice when unloading unsalvageable documents
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Step 18 of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#unload-a-document says

> Run any [unloading document cleanup steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#unloading-document-cleanup-steps) for oldDocument that are defined by this specification and [other applicable specifications](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/infrastructure.html#other-applicable-specifications).

Step 20 then says

> If oldDocument's [salvageable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#concept-document-salvageable) state is false, then [destroy](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#destroy-a-document) oldDocument.

As part of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#destroy-a-document step 6 states

> Run any [unloading document cleanup steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#unloading-document-cleanup-steps) for document that are defined by this specification and [other applicable specifications](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/infrastructure.html#other-applicable-specifications).

In other words, if the document is not salvageable, these steps run twice.

Should instead step 20 of https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#unload-a-document state in the else clause that it should run the steps and remove step 18? I am not sure if any of the unloading document steps set the salvagable of document to false, but it seems wrong to me to call these unloading steps twice.
